articles.detail: 5 cycles, all 5 completed, committed and deployed; each wrote 13, dedup and validation trimmed to ~11 published per cycle

experiment: Skipped — every goal metric is inside target, no experiment is active, and no pause gate applies. The one real defect today (a cross-cycle duplicate) lives in scripts/lib/dedup.js, which is not a tunable parameter in this scope, and no feed or floor parameter would have prevented it.
weakestArea: Duplicates. The 12:00 and 22:00 cycles both published the same SciDev.Net feature on Liberian contraceptive stockouts — identical source URL, ten hours apart. All four dedup layers missed it for a structural reason: the slugs share no words (a-health-system-held-as-a-subscription vs liberia-contraception-donor-funding-cuts) so layer 3 fails, and the titles share only 'Cuts' so layer 4's three-word recap threshold fails. Nothing in wouldDedup() compares source URLs, even though both stories carried the same one verbatim — a fifth layer keyed on normalised source URL would have caught this deterministically at zero token cost. Everything else is comfortable: freshness median 0.2 against a 1.0 target, sci-tech at 36%, top source at 13%.
watching: The dedup ladder has no source-URL layer, so an identical URL reframed with a fresh slug and headline passes cleanly — this is the third same-URL duplicate in three days (2 yesterday, 1 today) and every one would fall to an exact URL comparison.

acronymViolations sat at 379 in the latest weekly snapshot, but the top five violators are IR, PK, IN, RU and CN — the regex in measure-quality.js:128 scans the raw body, so it is counting the ISO-2 codes inside (country:XX) link markup, not unexpanded prose acronyms. The metric is measuring syntax and is not actionable as written.

Cycle health fully recovered from yesterday: 5 of 5 completed today against 1 of 5 on 2026-08-10, and the build-lock contention that cost four cycles is gone. Wall-time rose to 1371s average (selector 303s, writer 363s, editor 101s) — still far inside every timeout.

Article throughput fell 71 to 56 while the per-cycle written count held at 13, so the drop is downstream trimming rather than thin selection; worth a second day of observation before reading anything into it.

multiSourceRatePct in the weekly snapshot slipped 22.8 to 20.9. Two prior experiments established that the feed's ~9 multi-source clusters per cycle cap this near 22%, so the lever is upstream feed clustering, not the selector floors.
FIRMS_MAP_KEY is still absent from the systemd service file — the thermal snapshot skipped on all five cycles again and the map continues to serve a stale layer.
coverageGaps: Oceania produced a single article for the fifth consecutive day and remains the only region that never clears one.
Europe fell to 7 from 12 yesterday, the sharpest single-region swing of the day, while Africa rose to 10 — its strongest showing this week.
Science and tech tied at 10 each, both down from 13 and 19 yesterday; the ratio still clears 25% comfortably but the absolute floor for tech (3/cycle) is the binding constraint on light feed days.
Politics took 22 of 56 slots (39%), the widest category share of the day, though no stated target governs it.
context: A clean day on every measured axis: 56 articles across five completed cycles, freshness median 0.2 with a 1.3-day maximum, 39 unique sources with no outlet above 13%, six regions, and eight multi-source stories against a floor of four. The experiment slate is empty and stays empty — proposing a variable against metrics this healthy would only add noise. The queued numerical-density experiment remains blocked on its own preflight (replicate the n=3 bench gain at n>=20 first) and targets scripts/write-prompt.md, outside daily-tuning scope regardless. The two findings worth an operator decision both sit outside that scope: adding a source-URL layer to scripts/lib/dedup.js, and either excluding (country:XX) markup from the acronym regex in scripts/measure-quality.js or retiring the metric, since at present it reports a number that cannot go down.
